proof.criterion: Architect item 1a: with four overlapping pre-boot inserts on 5M ids, the first start reads a bounded number of rows and every event arrives once, in order.
proof.surface: /ws/live cold subscription on a newly started head process that a head process before it had served, 5,000,122 ids
proof.command: adv.py persisted head 3.0 0.5, twice (rows of events read = pg_stat seq_tup_read + events_pkey idx_tup_read around the start, other backends ended so their counts flush)

proof.criterion: Architect item 1b: a reset log (created_at mismatch) ignores the stored value; two processes writing it never move it backwards; a horizon persisted by a process that then died is still sound for the next one.
proof.surface: event_horizon, /auth/whoami and /ws/live across a truncate, two processes and a kill -9
proof.command: adv.py reset_persisted head; adv.py twoproc_persist 20; adv.py dead head; adv.py late_insert head
proof.observed: Reset: stored 122 from the old log; after `truncate events restart identity` and a 300-row refill, the new log's row 122 had another created_at. With an insert from before boot open, whoami answered 503 EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE after 2.1 s rather than the stale 122; the first start read the whole new log (warning logged); the insert g=301 and a comment h=302 committed after the start both arrived. Two processes under 20 s of load: 39 samples of event_horizon.safe, 22 distinct, from 122 to 1701, with no backward step; a write of id 50 through the persist statement left it at 1701. Dead process: one persisted 5000122 and was killed -9; the next, with an insert open since before boot, answered whoami 5000122 in 12 ms and read no whole log; the insert g=5000124 and a comment h=5000125 committed after the start each arrived once, in order. A write that took its xid before boot and inserted after the start: delivered once, in order.
proof.negativeControl: Round 13 (no persisted horizon): an insert from before boot made whoami answer 503 for as long as the insert stayed open.
